u1.detail: - **CdcStartPosition**: A parameter that specifies where a CDC operation should begin. It accepts formats like a timestamp, native database log position (e.g., LSN for SQL Server, SCN for Oracle), or a checkpoint string. Specifying both CdcStartPosition and CdcStartTime causes an error. [[4]](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/APIReference/API_StartReplicationTask.html) - **RecoveryCheckpoint**: A system-generated string in the ReplicationTask object that encodes the exact point (often in a vendor-specific format, e.g., `checkpoint:V1#...`) where DMS last safely processed changes. It is exposed in task descriptions and the console under the CDC section. [[1]](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/APIReference/API_ReplicationTask.html) 1. **Retrieve the value** — Use the AWS Console (task overview > CDC section), `DescribeReplicationTasks` API/CLI, or SDK to fetch the `RecoveryCheckpoint` from an existing task. [[3]](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Task.CDC.html)

u2.summary: **The `RecoveryCheckpoint` field in the `DescribeReplicationTasks` API (AWS Database Migration Service - DMS) indicates the last checkpoint recorded during a Change Data Capture (…
u2.detail: **The `RecoveryCheckpoint` field in the `DescribeReplicationTasks` API (AWS Database Migration Service - DMS) indicates the last checkpoint recorded during a Change Data Capture (CDC) operation for a replication task.** [1] - **Usage for Recovery**: Provide the `RecoveryCheckpoint` value to the `CdcStartPosition` parameter when starting or modifying a task (via `StartReplicationTask` or `ModifyReplicationTask`). This restarts CDC from that exact point. [3] - **Availability**: The value is most reliable when the task is in a **stopped** or **failed** state. It may not persist if the task is deleted. For some sources (e.g., PostgreSQL), you can also query the `awsdms_txn_state` metadata table on the target if `TaskRecoveryTableEnabled` is set to `true` in task settings. CdcStartTime or CdcStartPosition to specify when you want a CDC operation to start. `start-replication` is the only valid action that can be used for the first time a task with the migration type of `full-load`full-load, `full-load-and-cdc` or `cdc` is run. Any other action used for the first time on a given task, such as `resume-processing` and reload-target will result in data errors. You can also use [ReloadTables](./API_ReloadTables.html) to reload specific tables that failed during migration instead of restarting the task. For a `full-load-and-cdc` task, DMS migrates table data, and then applies data changes that occur on the source. To load all the tables again, and start capturing source changes, use `reload-target`. Otherwise use `resume-processing`, to replicate the changes from the last stop position. For a `cdc` only task, to start from a specific position, you must use start-replication and also specify the start position. Check the source endpoint DMS documentation for any limitations. What is RecoveryTimeout in change processing tuning, its default behavior, and impact on resume when checkpoint is not immediately encountered?
Any documented differences or best practices for checkpoint recovery across engines, especially Postgres?
